function: Estimation of the direct and cascaded user-IRS-BS channels in IRS-aided mmWave systems, using a deep-unfolded two-stage LAMP network with row compression (p. 1).
system: BS with 32-antenna ULA and hybrid precoding, single-antenna user, passive reflecting IRS with 64 elements (8x8 UPA), mmWave band, carrier frequency not given (pp. 3, 10).
method: Deep unfolding of AMP (LAMP, two stages, row compression, MMV variant); supervised end-to-end NMSE training, with transfer learning and fine-tuning in a three-stage procedure (pp. 5-9).
data_channel: Own simulator with Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave channels, 3 paths per link, uniform random angles; 10^5 training and 10^4 test samples per SNR; no public or measured data (pp. 3, 10).
test_conditions: Trained at SNR 5 dB, tested from -10 to 20 dB; same array sizes, paths and angle distribution in training and testing; T and grid oversampling varied (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Classical: TRICE-OMP (beta 1, 2, 8) and Oracle LS; learned: joint-CS LAMP network; the paper's own variants TS-LAMP, RCTS-LAMP-MMV and weight-sharing methods (p. 10).
metrics: NMSE of cascaded and direct channels, average receive signal power ratio (ARSPR), and execution time (pp. 10, 12).
complexity: Orders in Table II, e.g. O(LTQK_B + LT|Omega|K_S) for RCTS-LAMP; execution time 1.8 to 2.5 ms versus 24.5 ms for joint-CS LAMP (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 3: "We assume the widely used Saleh-Valenzuela (SV) channel model [27]". Custom simulator with distance-based path gains (p. 10); the paper never mentions 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "For both training and testing, the angular-domain path angles" are uniformly distributed. Training and testing share the simulator; only the SNR varies (train 5 dB, test -10 to 20 dB), a sweep that does not count. No new scenario, array size, or dataset is tested.
q3_support: p. 11: "achieving better NMSE performance than the LAMP network", the learned benchmark "Joint-CS recovery with LAMP network" of [26] defined on p. 10; p. 11: "can outperform TRICE-OMP", the non-learned benchmark.
q4_support: p. 12: "Table II shows that the TS-LAMP network effectively reduces the execution time by 83%". Table II gives complexity orders (RCTS-LAMP: O(LTQK_B + LT|Omega|K_S)) and execution times of 1.8 to 2.5 ms.
q5_support: p. 10: "We use the deep learning library PyTorch for the training and testing of the proposed networks." No code or data link, DOI, public dataset, or measured data is given; the samples come from the authors' own simulator.
notes: Included, area 2: joint estimation of direct and cascaded channels for passive IRS-aided mmWave; deep unfolding with trained parameters counts as learned. q3 is borderline: the only learned baseline is the joint-CS LAMP network of [26] that the authors implement (p. 10); TS-LAMP, the MMV variant and the weight-sharing methods are the paper's own variants and were not counted. q2: the transfer learning of the three-stage training (p. 9) adapts the first network to a different task (direct channel) with the same 10^5 samples, not to a new scenario, so it was not counted; Fig. 6 (p. 12) varies the number of blocks T and Fig. 5 (p. 11) the oversampling rate, but the paper never says that a network trained for one T or rate is tested at another. Table II (p. 12) was read from the page image.
